summary: TechCrunch reports, citing multiple sources, that Palo Alto Networks is in advanced but unclosed talks to buy two Israeli security startups, Talon Cyber Security and Dig Security, for about $1 billion combined. The article places the deals in broader cybersecurity trends: renewed security spending, AI-driven threats, startup acquisitions by larger firms, and a swing toward large platforms. It also raises the question of how Palo Alto will integrate its many acquisitions into a coherent product.
one_line: Palo Alto Networks is reportedly in advanced talks to buy Israeli startups Talon ($600-700M) and Dig Security ($300-400M) for about $1B total.
key_facts: Palo Alto Networks is in advanced negotiations to buy two Israeli security startups, Talon Cyber Security and Dig Security, for around $1 billion altogether; the deals are not yet closed.
Talon Cyber Security, which built an enterprise browser aimed at securing distributed workforces, would be bought for between $600 million and $700 million.
Dig Security, a specialist in securing data across public clouds, would be bought for between $300 million and $400 million.
Palo Alto Networks is publicly traded with a market cap of close to $70 billion.
Both Talon and Dig are less than three years old; Talon has raised around $143 million and Dig only around $45 million.
Talon and Dig share investors Team8 and Cyverse Capital; Dig's investors also include Signal Fire, Okta, CrowdStrike, Samsung and Felicis.
Palo Alto approached both startups proactively; neither was in the market to be acquired.
Israeli publication Calcalist reported on both deals in the past week with the same figures.
A McKinsey report says breaches are on track to cost $10.5 trillion annually by 2025, a 300% increase on 2015 figures.
Comparable deals include CrowdStrike buying Bionic for $350 million, IBM buying Polar for $60 million, and Cisco's planned $28 billion purchase of Splunk.
IBM's Polar purchase was reportedly partly a response to Palo Alto buying Cider Security in 2022.
Wiz, a competitor now valued at $10 billion, and Island, another enterprise browser company, are named as competitive threats.
Palo Alto has more than 30 products and services and has made 17 acquisitions in total; some departing customers say 'they feel like the product is disconnected'.
